summary: 1. Focus topics on visceral body phenomena and immediate sensory traps rather than standard pantry trivia like honey or maple syrup. 2. Start script hooks instantly with a direct second-person contradiction or aggressive statement within the first 8 words. 3. Title videos using visceral action verbs and bodily consequences like 'Eat You Back' or 'Secretly Leaking' to maximize feed CTR. 4. Target optimal video duration between 18 to 22 seconds, which balances high stayed rate with strong view percentage. 5. Completely strip out introductory fluff, textbook explanations, and rhetorical setup questions from second 0.
winning_hooks: Direct bodily paradoxes that confront the viewer immediately ('Your fingers prune in water, but it is not because...')
Aggressive personification of everyday items ('Fresh pineapple is literally eating you back')
Extreme comparative anchors ('This shark is older than the United States')
avoid: Passive, encyclopedic openings like 'Honey is famous for being one of the only...'
Rhetorical fluff questions at second 0 like 'That sweet maple syrup on your pancakes?'
Long explanatory clauses that give away technical reasons before establishing a paradox
next_experiment: A/B test a body-anomaly video topic ('Why Stomach Acid Doesn't Melt You'): Version A opens with an aggressive direct statement ('Your stomach is currently digesting itself') vs. Version B opening with a fact setup ('Stomach acid is strong enough to burn through wood'), keeping length at 18 seconds to measure stayed_pct lift.
